claims.quote: Now she’s 30, and her private, Palo Alto-based corporation, called Theranos–the name is an amalgam of the words “therapy” and “diagnosis”–has 500 employees and has raised more than $400 million from equity sales to investors who have effectively valued the company at more than $9 billion.
claims.why: Check the employee count, funds raised, and company valuation with Theranos financial records.

claims.quote: Theranos today is a potentially highly disruptive upstart in America’s $73 billion diagnostic-lab industry, which performs nearly 10 billion tests a year and is estimated to provide the basis for about 70% of doctors’ medical decisions.
claims.why: Verify the total size of the US diagnostic-lab industry and annual test volume statistics.

claims.quote: Theranos runs what’s called a high-complexity laboratory, certified by the federal Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), and it is licensed to operate in nearly every state.
claims.why: Check CMS certification status and state operating licenses for Theranos.

claims.quote: It currently offers more than 200–and is ramping up to offer more than 1,000–of the most commonly ordered blood diagnostic tests, all without the need for a syringe.
claims.why: Verify the exact number of blood tests currently offered by Theranos.

claims.quote: The company has performed as many as 70 different tests from a single draw of 25 to 50 microliters collected in a tiny vial the size of an electric fuse, which Holmes has dubbed a “nanotainer.”
claims.why: Check if running 70 tests on 25 microliters is verified by independent laboratories.

claims.quote: Its prices are often a half to a quarter of what independent labs charge, and a quarter to a 10th of what hospital labs bill, with still greater savings for expensive procedures.
claims.why: Compare Theranos test pricing against independent and hospital laboratory prices.

claims.quote: Precisely how Theranos accomplishes all these amazing feats is a trade secret.
claims.why: Check if technical explanations are withheld under the justification of trade secrets.

claims.quote: Holmes will only say–and this is more than she has ever said before–that her company uses “the same fundamental chemical methods” as existing labs did.
claims.why: Verify whether technical answers regarding test execution methods are overly generic.

claims.quote: Its phlebotomists currently take physician-ordered blood draws (and saliva, urine, feces, and other samples) at collection centers the company operates at its headquarters in Palo Alto and at 21 Walgreens–one in Palo Alto and the rest in Phoenix.
claims.why: Count the exact number of operational Walgreens wellness centers mentioned.

claims.quote: Using DNA profiling Theranos can, for less than the cost of the conventional tests, identify a bug and its resistance profile within four hours, says Helfet, according to the data he has seen.
claims.why: Check the validity of DNA profiling turnaround times and costs cited by Helfet.

claims.quote: Holmes counters that because, as noted, her tests employ “the same fundamental chemical methods” as existing tests, peer-review publication of validation studies is both unnecessary and inappropriate.
claims.why: Check if peer-reviewed validation studies are missing for Theranos assays.

claims.quote: Theranos may, in fact, be the only lab to have ever sought FDA clearance for LDTs.
claims.why: Check FDA records to verify if Theranos is unique in seeking clearance for LDTs.

claims.quote: In a rare if not unprecedented rout this past March, the patent holders unconditionally surrendered midtrial, stipulating to the invalidity of their own patent.
claims.why: Verify court records regarding the patent settlement mentioned.

claims.quote: Today Holmes is a co-inventor on 82 U.S. and 189 foreign patent applications, of which 18 in the U.S. and 66 abroad have been granted.
claims.why: Check US and international patent office databases for Holmes patent filings.

claims.quote: Though she has now raised more than $400 million, she says she has retained control over more than 50% of the stock.
claims.why: Verify stock ownership percentages and total capital raised.

claims.quote: Theranos would test drug-trial subjects three times a week–which wouldn’t have been feasible using venipuncture–and catch adverse drug effects quickly, before they became dangerous.
claims.why: Check if pharmaceutical partners independently validated frequent micro-sample drug trial testing.

claims.quote: Theranos is a potentially highly disruptive upstart in America’s diagnostic-lab industry.
claims.why: Verify subjective market disruption claims lacking concrete operational metrics.

claims.quote: She has assembled what, in terms of public service at least, may be the single most accomplished board in U.S. corporate history.
claims.why: Assess the subjective praise regarding the corporate board's historical significance.

claims.quote: Such pricing represents a potential godsend for the uninsured, the insured with high deductibles, insurers, and taxpayers.
claims.why: Verify broad assertions about economic relief without specific savings calculations.

claims.quote: She is like a monk.
claims.why: Check metaphorical descriptions of personal lifestyle and temperament.
